owner_identity.meet_bridge: The Meet Worker derives the address from its verified owner session and uses the existing signed Core owner exchange. Core resolves that identity; no request accepts a caller-supplied email or user id as authority.
owner_identity.unmapped_owner: Do not create a Core identity or assign favorites by guess. Report the owner as unmapped for recovery.

storage.target_metadata: Resolve current names, titles, icons, and destinations through the owning service. Never copy them or Docs content into the favorites relation.
storage.missing_target: Omit it from rendered lists, keep the favorite reference, and allow it to resolve again if the target returns.
storage.writes: Add and remove are idempotent. Re-adding a removed target starts a new created_at; adding an existing target does not reorder it.

eligible.reference: Core lead UUID, canonical lowercase UUID.
eligible.resolver: Resolve by id through the owner's authorized CRM subject read, including a subject no longer in the open Work list.
eligible.access: The existing member CRM read capability; a favorite grants no access.

eligible.reference: Core project UUID, canonical lowercase UUID.
eligible.resolver: Resolve by id through the owner's authorized CRM subject read, including a subject no longer in the open Work list.
eligible.access: The existing member CRM read capability; a favorite grants no access.

eligible.reference: Core organization UUID, canonical lowercase UUID.
eligible.resolver: Resolve by id through the owner's authorized CRM subject read.
eligible.access: The existing member CRM read capability; a favorite grants no access.

eligible.reference: CMS events.id UUID, canonical lowercase UUID.
eligible.resolver: Resolve by id, not only from the upcoming/open event projection.
eligible.access: The existing member event read capability; a favorite grants no access.
eligible.lifecycle: Closing, passing, or demoting an event never deletes its favorite. An unavailable event is omitted until its owning read can resolve it again.

eligible.eligibility: An allowlisted entity is eligible only while the member's current registry grants read access and CoreKit has an authorized record-by-id resolver and detail destination. Adding a registry entity does not automatically add a favorite kind target.
eligible.resolver: CoreKit CRMRepository.record(entity:id:) under the member's current entity view capability.
eligible.destination: The owning Core registry detail view. Meet Mac/iOS and Core helper can host it through CoreKit. Meet web omits Core records until it has a working Core detail destination.
eligible.access: Recheck the current registry read/view permission on every resolve and open.

eligible.reference: Core task UUID, canonical lowercase UUID.
eligible.resolver: Resolve by id through the authorized task read.
eligible.access: The current task read capability; starring does not assign, reopen, or change stage.
eligible.rationale: A personal shortcut remains useful regardless of assignment or stage; starring does not change workflow state.

eligible.resolver: Resolve through the current linked-repository issue read.
eligible.access: Recheck repository and issue access. Starring does not change labels, assignee, or state.
eligible.rationale: A personal shortcut remains useful regardless of assignee or issue state; starring does not change workflow state.
eligible.lifecycle: A moved or inaccessible issue is omitted while its reference remains stored.

eligible.reference: Docs document UUID in lowercase (not title, slug, or path).
eligible.resolver: Resolve through the authenticated Docs document read.
eligible.access: Apply Docs' normal member visibility and grant checks.
eligible.lifecycle: Rename and move keep the document id; the resolver supplies its current title and path.

eligible.reference: Docs folder UUID in lowercase (never the mutable path).
eligible.resolver: Resolve folder id to its current path from the authenticated Docs tree/read API.
eligible.access: Apply Docs' normal member visibility and grant checks to its contents.
eligible.lifecycle: Rename/move preserves the folder id and changes the resolved path. Deletion leaves an unresolved reference; recreating the same path creates a different favorite target.

eligible.reference: The durable people.sub principal, not the mutable email address.
eligible.resolver: Resolve the principal through the member-gated roster, then build the current person row and email-based door.
eligible.access: Use the current Team directory visibility and person actions.

eligible.reference: The agent's stable AGENT_ROSTER sub, not its email suffix.
eligible.resolver: Resolve through the current member-gated agent roster, then build the current agent row and message door.
eligible.access: A favorite grants no session, authority, or thread membership. Keep agent distinct from person.

eligible.resolver: Resolve only through the caller's current member thread list.
eligible.access: Recheck thread membership; a favorite never grants membership.
eligible.message_hit: A message search hit targets its containing thread, never the individual message.

aliases.favorite_target: Their parent CRM subject until a direct detail destination exists.
docs.document when the owning Docs document is the opened object.

deferred_or_excluded.decision: Calendar events are not favorite targets. CMS events use cms.event and are starred from Work.
Calendar events are not favorite targets. EventKit identifiers are also only best-effort on the same device and are not promised stable across devices.
Defer until the subscription id plus UID/recurrence identity is exposed and verified through a cross-client resolver.
Exclude until the Core registry supplies a stable record id, authorized by-id resolver, and destination. A list-only registry category is not a favorite target.
Not independent targets while their existing door opens only the parent subject.
Not an independent target; favorite the containing conversation.
Defer until it has a stable independent destination. A note that is a Docs document uses docs.document.
Never a favorite target. Meet does not record audio or video.
Not an entity; these are places and actions rather than durable records.

migration.timestamp: Use updated_at as the best available legacy order. It can reflect a later mute edit as well as a star because the old row has no separate starred_at. Preserve the row and report that ordering limitation; never silently discard it.
migration.compatibility: Keep GET/PUT /api/crm/subject-state and GET /api/crm/starred as adapters until old clients are outside the rollback window.

reference_contract.stable_ui_key: Join the canonical kind, one colon, and target_ref. Split only at the first colon because references may contain colons.
reference_contract.uuid: Canonical lowercase UUID text. Core normalizes UUID references to lowercase before storage.
reference_contract.opaque_principal: meet.person and meet.agent use their durable principal key exactly; reject whitespace and control characters.
reference_contract.github_issue: Store owner and repo in lowercase so case-insensitive GitHub paths have one favorite identity.
reference_contract.core_record: The entity id must be on the explicit current registry allowlist; if native_record_id is a UUID, store it lowercase.
